newsitem.title: THAILAND: SITCA seeks to restart bank talks.
newsitem.headline: SITCA seeks to restart bank talks.

text.p: SITCA Invesment and Securities Plc said Wednesaday it was prepared to discuss new proposals to restart stalled takeover talks with Thai authorities for ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce.

SITCA's senior executives indicated that they were prepared to consider increasing the firm's offer for 60 percent of the bank's stock, the key sticking point on which talks were said to have broken down.

SITCA and the state-appointed control committee handling the sale of BBC, which collapsed in May with non-performing loans of 85 billion baht, are said to have agreed that SITCA will buy an initial 30 percent stake in the bank for 10 baht per share.
But problems arose when the control committee asked for 32 baht per share for the second 30 percent stake. SITCA had offered to pay 20 baht per share.
"32 baht for 30 percent of the shares is okay so long as the authorities clarify how they set the price," SITCA's President of Securities Warapatr Todhanakasem told reporters.
He said SITCA was seeking clarification of the structure of the banks' supervisory and executive boards, another sticking point in negotiations, he said.

His comments softened SITCA's earlier hard line when in response to media reports it issued a statement condemning the control committee for altering takeover terms as the two sides were approaching agreement at the end of November.
"The goal posts were moved and new conditions imposed by the control committee," said the company.
Representatives from the control committee were not immediately available for comment.
Failure to reach agreement with SITCA, could lead to negotiations being opened with rival bidder Nithipat Capital Plc, or leave the central bank as the largest shareholder in BBC.

SITCA's nine member takeover consortium, which includes Thai Petrochemical Industry and TOA Paint, had an application for a commercial bank for a commercial bank licence turned down earlier this year by the authorities. (US$1 = 25.5 baht)
